evidence_note: v1 remains the headline. v2 was chosen after the result was known and is sensitivity-only.

market_classification.definition: eventual outcome >= 0.90 at the first minute at/after official poll close and never below 0.80 afterwards

mix.label: tau mixture over earlier nights (chosen after the result was known)
mix.note: An equal-weight mixture over the reporting-order errors that 8 earlier count nights needed (mx2012 0.015, mx2018 0.02, br2022r1 0, br2022r2 0.005, mx2024 0.03, pl2025r1 0.0075, pl2025r2 0.02, br2026r1 0.015). Same point forecast as the base model (rho 0.8, kappa 50,000); only the band and the win chance allow for those 8 different errors instead of one. Built from earlier nights only, but chosen after this result was known, so it is a sensitivity, not a forecast.

v2.label: v2: settings from 2014, 2018 and 2022 (chosen after the result was known)

accuracy.pwin_window: minutes from >= 1% of the race counted until both model and market stayed >= 0.9 on the winner (model only where no prices survive)

profit.rule: frozen night rule: favoured side only, edge >= 5c after costs, >= 1% of the market counted, first signal per market, held to resolution
profit.execution: real taker trades on our side at or better than the signal price, from 60 s to 30 min after the signal; return at the signal's all-in cost (price + half-spread + fee)

invest10k.execution: model limit: after the 1% gate, 10% of every real taker trade (Israel: resting ask in the recorded book) on the favoured side whose all-in price leaves the model >= 5c, using the model P known >= 60 s earlier; no per-market cap
invest10k.note: Single event: every bet depends on the same election-night count, so the markets move together and this is one outcome, not many independent bets. 99% of the eligible volume was in one market (will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-the-2026-brazilian-presidential-election). Eligible volume is an upper bound: other traders took those trades.

signal_price.execution: real taker trades on our side at or better than the signal price, from 60 s to 30 min after the signal; cost = signal price + half-spread + taker fee
